learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of the basic principles of fluid mechanics and its application to problem-solving in the field of engineering. Calculation of pipes, channels, and fluid systems.
Applied knowledge of the fundamentals of fluid-mechanical systems and machines.
Designs and dimensions piping networks, ducts, and elements in an installation.
Analyzes fluid distribution networks using specific computational tools.
Identifies, diagnoses, and proposes solutions to real problems that arise in fluid distribution networks.
Understands the operation and is capable of selecting fluid-mechanical machines according to the characteristics of the distribution system.
Designs and dimensions suitable fluid-mechanical machines for real distribution systems.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans, and other similar tasks.
Ability to handle mandatory specifications, regulations, and standards.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Knowledge, understanding, and ability to apply the necessary legislation in the exercise of the profession of Industrial Technical Engineer.

syllabus_topics: Flow in ducts: equations, dimensioning, elements, instrumentation
Design, selection, dimensioning, and integration of fluid-mechanical machines in networks
Diagnosis and maintenance of distribution networks
Practical project: integral design of a distribution network
Trends and emerging technologies in fluid networks

assessment_methods.method: Practices (attendance, participation, data processing and analysis)
Team practical assignment (creativity, calculations, optimization, presentation)

assessment_rules: Evaluation is based on practices (30%) and a team practical assignment (70%). If the student does not pass these activities during the semester, they will have the opportunity to pass the subject through a global test (100%) in the ordinary or extraordinary calls. The use of unpermitted materials or electronic devices during evaluation may lead to exam withdrawal and a failing grade (0).
